title: Update: Redesigned the UI based on your feedback (Narrowed down to 5 options!)
author: hwantasticgames
selftext:
I’m back just a day later! Yesterday, I posted an introduction to promote my game, and many of you pointed out that the UI looked way too "AI-generated." Looking back, no wonder the promo didn't land well.

So today, I experimented with several different designs and narrowed it down to about five candidates. Right before writing this, I was leaning toward going with **Option D**.

You might find the other options more aesthetically pleasing, and honestly, I agree that some of them might look prettier. However, here’s why Option D is my top pick: the other candidates feel too much like a traditional casino game. Since I envision this game's core identity as a board game, I felt the UI needed to stay as casual as possible.

I'd really appreciate your feedback with this context in mind!

comments.author: scratchieee
comments.body: I think this looks like you asked an LLM to reskin it and it used the 5 generic themes LLMs will recolor to. I think the problem with the game is it looks like you just asked the agent to build it and aren't defining unique styles. #3 looks best by far but there are multiple posts of this exact game every hour on this sub

comments.author: NovaGuarda
comments.body: So you think you'd fix the llm look by asking an llm to fix it?

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body: there must be a reason why llm games dont make millions yet

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: d for me, with the color of c or e

comments.author: JohtoBorn
comments.body: I think you need to spend a lot more time working through the design. I think you can easily get something that looks less like an llm made it with some more directed prompts.

comments.author: rollinff
comments.body: The challenge with this is LLMs are great at visual design, so you're going to get a design that you look at and say oh this looks good without realizing 1,000 people are getting the same great looking results. Now you all look the same, and players pattern match. Something in most of our brains detect that pattern and now just think, nope. Even if the design itself is good in a vacuum.
